llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose, required files, and runtime instructions are internally consistent with a local-invocation CLI-based security tool, but you must trust the upstream GitHub code before installing and be aware of some operational tradeoffs (local key storage, audit hashing, and a deliberate downgrade policy).

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required binary (python3), and the declared config paths (~/.openclaw360/*) align with a local CLI security tool. No unrelated cloud credentials or system-wide resources are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to local CLI invocations (check-prompt, check-tool, scan-skills, backup/restore, etc.) and to reading/writing files under ~/.openclaw360/. The skill also instructs scanning user-specified skill directories (scan-skills), which means the agent will read whatever path you point it at — that can expose file contents present there. Audit logs are said to retain only SHA-256 hashes of sensitive values (no raw values), but unsalted hashing can be vulnerable to brute-force/dictionary attacks for low-entropy secrets. The skill documents a deliberate downgrade behavior: if checks fail it will continue execution after notifying the user — a security/usability tradeoff you should accept consciously.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is via pip installing a GitHub commit (git+https://github.com/...@<commit>). This is a common pattern and the commit hash is pinned (better than an unpinned install), but installing remote code requires trusting the upstream repo; there is no bundled code in the registry entry to audit automatically.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. The tool creates and uses local files (config, Ed25519 identity keys, audit logs) under ~/.openclaw360/, which is proportionate for a local security/audit utility. Users should note the presence of a local private key (identity/) used for signing manifests and logs — protect that directory (0600 is recommended).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and disable-model-invocation:true mean the skill will not be auto-invoked by the platform and does not demand permanent agent presence. It writes only to its own ~/.openclaw360/ directory and describes no background processes, autorun, or network callbacks in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for a local CLI-based runtime security tool, but before installing you should: (1) manually review the GitHub repository at the pinned commit to verify behavior matches the SKILL.md claims (especially the 'no network' and 'no telemetry' assertions); (2) be comfortable that running pip install from GitHub is a trust decision — consider installing into an isolated virtualenv; (3) understand that the tool will create an Ed25519 private key under ~/.openclaw360/identity/ (treat that like any private key); (4) be aware that audit logs keep only SHA-256 hashes of sensitive values — hashing without salt can be reversible for low-entropy secrets; (5) when using scan-skills, only point it at directories you intend it to read because it will analyze files you specify. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a reproducible release artifact (signed release or package registry entry) or request a third-party code audit of the pinned commit.
